mo[mo=="~1"]

If I run the above code it will return an empty list.

character(0)

That is because you are missing a comma, indicating that you are selecting rows of the data.frame mo, but returning all the columns.

mo[mo=="~1" , ]
I checked again and tried to return all the indices, the intercepts are not included.

You did not provide your full script, but I would guess that you did not include a mean structure.  Did you set the argument "meanstructure = TRUE"?

Terry

messages.author: fbde11873d6580ef
messages.subject: Re: modification indices do not include intercepts
parts: Thanks for your suggestions, Terry. I have the same problem. I tried your advice:
Did you set the argument "meanstructure = TRUE"?

That does not seem to help. Using lavaan 0.5-18, I do het MIs for intercepts, but not in lavaan 0.5-20. Maybe I'm missing something here.

Working example:

manic.cov <- lav_matrix_lower2full(c(9.364, 7.777, 12.461, 6.422,  8.756, 10.112))
manic.means <- c(10.09, 12.07, 10.25)
norm.cov <- lav_matrix_lower2full(c(9.610, 5.844, 8.410, 6.324, 6.264, 9.000))
norm.means <- c(10.10, 10.30, 9.80)

wisc3.names <- c("Info", "Sim", "Vocab")
colnames(manic.cov) <- rownames(manic.cov)  <- names(manic.means) <- colnames(norm.cov) <- rownames(norm.cov)  <- names(norm.means) <- wisc3.names

combined.cov <- list(manic=manic.cov, norm=norm.cov)
combined.n <- list(manic=81, norm=200)
combined.means <- list(manic=manic.means, norm=norm.means)

wisc3.model <- 'IQ =~ Info + Sim + Vocab'

strong.fit <- cfa(wisc3.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means,
                  meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))

modindices(strong.fit, op="~1", sort=T) # empty list
modindices(strong.fit) # no MIs for intercepts
summary(strong.fit) # intercepts are in the model, and restricted to equality

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: modification indices do not include intercepts
parts: That does not seem to help. Using lavaan 0.5-18, I do het MIs for intercepts, but not in lavaan 0.5-20.

Thanks for the example.  I noticed a few other details that might be helpful for finding out where the issue is.

If I use labels, and cut the "intercepts" out of the group.equal argument, I see MIs for the latent intercepts, but still none for indicator intercepts.
wisc3.model <- 'IQ =~ Info + Sim + Vocab

Info ~ t1*1
Sim ~ t2*1
Vocab ~ t3*1
'
strong.fit <- cfa(wisc3.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means, meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal="loadings")
modindices(strong.fit, op = "~1", sort = TRUE)

When I actually constrain the intercepts to fixed values, I end up seeing MIs for all intercepts.
wisc3.model <- 'IQ =~ Info + Sim + Vocab

Info + Sim + Vocab ~ 0*1
'
strong.fit <- cfa(wisc3.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means, meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal="loadings")
modindices(strong.fit, op = "~1", sort = TRUE)

So in the meantime, you could get MIs by fixing them to the estimated values from the strong-invariance model.  The mod indices might be a little smaller than they should be, since the model will have 3 fewer degrees of freedom than it should.  But I don't imagine the bias is big relative to the size of MI you might consider noteworthy, nor that the EPCs are would be noticeably biased.

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: modification indices do not include intercepts
parts:
On 11/24/2015 03:31 PM, Bunga Citra Pratiwi Asnawi wrote:
> With the new version of the lava an package the modification indices
> could not return intercepts.
>

> /mo <- modindices(strong.fit)/

This is due to a change in 0.5-19. From the release notes:

"the function modindices() will now only show modification indices for
newly added parameters; to assess the impact of releasing equality
constraints, use the function lavTestScore()"

So 'modindices()' now only shows modification indices for 'new'
parameters that were not included in the original model. It does not
show modification indices for (equality)-constrained parameters. In your
example, the intercepts were constrained by the group.equal="intercepts"
argument.

To see the effect of 'releasing' these equality constraints, you should
use the (new) lavTestScore() function. This will give you a 'global'
(multivariate) score test (aka the Lagrange Multiplier test), as well as
univariate and cumulative score tests for releasing a single constraint
at a time. Finally, you can also see how the other variables of the
model will change, if you release all the constraints.

Yves.
